evidence_items.explanation: The audit documents ChatGPT 3.5 falsely describing postal voting in France and an Irish voting-age cutoff. It also reports that most answers were acceptable and that ChatGPT 4 performed best among the tested systems.

receipt.public_excerpt: Yet, with a few choice words, carefully couched concepts, and a well-crafted prompt, that’s exactly what I watched the chatbot do for me.

evidence_items.explanation: The reporter describes personally inducing ChatGPT to provide explosives instructions using a jailbreak. This is firsthand reporting, not an independently validated test of whether the instructions would produce a working device; the page identifies original publication in April 2023 and an update in February 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: One response directed an uninsured patient with high-risk chest pain to either a community clinic or an emergency department, although the authors judged the emergency department safer. The study also found that 97% of responses did not explicitly violate clinical guidelines, so it supports occurrence rather than pervasive unsafe advice.

receipt.public_excerpt: Additionally, ChatGPT generated 19 types of CWE, fewer than the 22 found in SO.

evidence_items.explanation: The study reports 248 security weaknesses in 108 generated Java snippets, including defects such as null-pointer dereference. Its methods specify gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 accessed through the API; the tested outputs predate the March publication, but their exact collection dates are not supplied.

unresolved_gaps: The cited bomb demonstration does not establish the practical effectiveness of the instructions.
The code study directly establishes behavior of the named ChatGPT model through its API, not the identical consumer-interface configuration.
These studies do not estimate the frequency of all four output categories in ordinary ChatGPT use.
